newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela July imports rise 8.4 pct month on month.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela July imports rise 8.4 pct month on month.

text.p: The value of Venezuelan imports rose 8.4 percent in July to $978 million compared to $902 million in June, according to the Central Office of Statistics and Information (OCEI).

Imports also rose 14.5 percent on a year-on-year basis from $854 million in July 1995. Over the first seven months of the year, however, total imports were down 8.1 percent to $5.37 billion compared to $5.59 billion over the same period in 1995, OCEI said in a press release.
An overvalued currency saw imports in Venezuela rise 45 percent to $11.156 billion last year.

Over this year's January to July period, U.S. exports accounted for the lion's share, with a 43 percent, or $2.28 billion, market share. Colombia and Brazil followed with 8.5 percent and 4.8 percent shares, their exports respectively rising 34 percent to $459 million and 104 percent to $259 million, year on year.
Among European exporters, Germany accounted for 4.8 percent of Venezuelan imports, Italy 3.6 percent and France 2.1 percent. Imports from Japan accounted for 4.1 percent of the seven-month total.
Electrical goods made up the largest single import category, at 28.3 percent, or $1.52 billion, while chemical products accounted for 14.2 percent, or $762 million.
Over the period, the private sector remained far and away the largest importer, accounting for 86 percent or $4.62 million of total imports.
